body: In the future please do not upload individual files, MRPs should be archived

Likely the same root issue as https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/118804

CC @BastiaanOlij This seems to be a memory leak in your MSAA and 3D scaling code. I think it would be good to fix it in 4.8 since we expect all mobile developers to use 3D scaling

Adding a data point from another GPU vendor (Adreno), in case it helps triage.

- Device: Samsung Galaxy S23 Ultra (SM-S918B), Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 / Adreno 740, Android 16, display 1440x3088
- Engine: Godot v4.7.2.stable.official [ed1daf0bf], Compatibility renderer, debug export
- Driver: OpenGL ES 3.2 V@0676.77.1; it exposes `GL_EXT_multisampled_render_to_texture`

Same in-game 3D scene for each setting, set on the root viewport (no glow, SSAO or adjustments in the
Environment), app restarted between settings, `dumpsys meminfo` sampled about every 2.4 s for ~92 s.
Values from 10 s to the end of the run:

| `msaa_3d` | `scaling_3d_scale` | Native heap | GL mtrack |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2x | 0.9 | 192 -> 630 MB (+5.4 MB/s) | +0.45 MB/s |
| 2x | 1.0 | 137 -> 139 MB (flat) | flat |
| off | 0.75 | 137 -> 137 MB (flat) | flat |

A shorter repeat of MSAA 2x + 0.9 grew at 5.0 MB/s. So it is the same pattern as the Mali report: memory
only grows when MSAA is combined with a scale below 1.0, on a second GPU vendor.

This fits the path #118804 targets: with `rt_msaa_supported`, `_check_render_buffers()` takes the
`use_internal_buffer` MSAA branch and calls `glGenFramebuffers(1, &msaa3d.fbo)` again on every call,
because the early-out checks `msaa3d.color`, which that branch never sets
(`render_scene_buffers_gles3.cpp` lines 201, 271 and 381 at 4.7.2-stable).

> CC [@BastiaanOlij](https://github.com/BastiaanOlij) This seems to be a memory leak in your MSAA and 3D scaling code. I think it would be good to fix it in 4.8 since we expect all mobile developers to use 3D scaling

I've got it on my list of todos, just haven't gotten to it yet.

This code can follow several paths depending on whether the hardware can do tile based MSAA resolve using OpenGL vendor extensions, or has to fall back on us allocating MSAA buffers and performing a resolve ourselves.

If `rt_msaa_supported` is true, that is where the driver takes care of things and indeed as @kanevbg mentions, `msaa3d.color` would never be set as we never allocate a buffer.  The MSAA data never leaves tile memory and we save heaps of bandwidth.

When msaa is on, and scaling is disabled, we render MSAA in tile memory only, resolve in tile memory, then write out to our render target buffer.

When msaa is off, and scaling is enabled, we render into a lower res intermediate buffer, which gets scaled up to our render target bufffer.

When both are enabled, we render MSAA on tile, resolve and write into our intermediate buffer, then scaled up our intermediate buffer and write into our render target buffers.

My guess at this point would be that the code is getting confused around the intermediate buffer being setup for MSAA and re-allocating that.
@sandrobibi-bibi it would be good if you can test my fix and see if it resolves your issue.
I can confirm this on Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra (Android 17). https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/124643 fixes the issue on my end.
